title: Pointed etale maps identify ordinary henselizations and their quotients
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be an etale homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ be prime with preimage $\mathfrak p\subset A$, and suppose the induced residue map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism. For each of the local rings $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $T=C_{\mathfrak q}$ an ordinary henselization exists. The pair henselization of $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ is a henselian local ring $R^h$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_RR^h$, unchanged residue field, and the universal property for local maps to henselian local rings; the same holds for $T$. For any such choices, the canonical local map
$$\alpha:R^h\longrightarrow T^h$$
extending $R\to T\to T^h$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is characterized by extending the unique pointed $A$-algebra map $C\to R^h$ inducing the inverse of the given residue-field isomorphism. For every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, $\alpha$ identifies $IR^h$ with $IC\,T^h$ and induces an isomorphism
$$R^h/IR^h\xrightarrow{\sim}T^h/IC\,T^h$$
commuting with the structure maps from $A/I$ and $C/IC$. These quotients are ordinary henselizations of $(A/I)_{\mathfrak p/I}$ and $(C/IC)_{\mathfrak q/IC}$ respectively. Here an ordinary henselization is specified by the initial local map to a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]; pair henselization is the etale pair-colimit construction of [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], henselian terminology is [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and etaleness, localization and residue fields are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(T,\mathfrak m_T)$; for their pair-colimits $H_R,H_T$, [lem-trf-prime-pair-colimit-ind-etale-model] (for $A,\mathfrak p$ and for $C,\mathfrak q$) shows that each is a filtered colimit of etale algebras over the base ring, henselian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_RH_R$, resp. $\mathfrak m_TH_T$, with local structure map and structural residue-field isomorphism. Ordinary universal property of $H_R$: given a henselian local $S$ and a local map $g:R\to S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] over the base $R$ to the filtered etale colimit $H_R$, its prime $\mathfrak m_RH_R$ (lying over $\mathfrak m_R=g^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)$), and the unique $\kappa(\mathfrak m_R)$-map $H_R/\mathfrak m_RH_R\cong\kappa(\mathfrak m_R)\to S/\mathfrak m_S$. Every local $R$-map $H_R\to S$ has that maximal-ideal preimage and induces that residue map, so uniqueness among local maps follows; likewise for $H_T$. Hence ordinary henselizations exist, and this proves the assertions about the pair constructions. For any other ordinary henselization $R^h$, [lem-trf-initial-henselian-colimit-comparison] (with $C=H_R$, $H=R^h$) gives unique mutually inverse local $R$-maps $H_R\rightleftarrows R^h$; the same applies to $T^h$. An isomorphism carries the unique maximal ideal to the unique maximal ideal and commutes with the base-ring maps; hence these arbitrary choices have the same maximal-ideal and structural residue-field descriptions.

source.place: Tags 0A02 (lemma-henselization), 0A03 (lemma-henselization-local-ring); transfer to arbitrary initial choices by uniqueness

proof.text: Write $i:R\to R^h$ and $j:T\to T^h$ for the structure maps. The map $r:R\to T$ sends $a/s$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$; denominators are outside $\mathfrak q$, and the maximal-ideal preimage is $\mathfrak pR$, so $r$ is local. Initiality gives a unique local $\alpha:R^h\to T^h$ with $\alpha i=jr$. Identify the residue field of $R^h$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ using step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] to the single etale $A$-algebra $C$, the henselian local target $R^h$, the prime $\mathfrak q$ and the inverse $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of the given residue isomorphism. Its compatibility over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is exactly the inverse identity. We obtain a unique pointed $A$-map $f:C\to R^h$ with $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{R^h})=\mathfrak q$. Every $c\notin\mathfrak q$ maps to a unit, so $b(c/s)=f(c)f(s)^{-1}$ defines a unique local map $b:T\to R^h$. Its restriction to $R$ is $i$, since both send $a/s$ to $i(a)i(s)^{-1}$. Initiality for $T^h$ now gives a unique local $\beta:T^h\to R^h$ with $\beta j=b$.

source.place: Tag 08HQ (lemma-map-into-henselian); localization at the specified prime and initial local-map universal properties

proof.text: The composite $\beta\alpha$ is a local $R$-map on $R^h$, since $\beta\alpha i=\beta jr=br=i$; initiality gives $\beta\alpha=1$. For the other composite, compare the two $A$-maps $C\to T^h$ given by the structural map $C\to T\xrightarrow{j}T^h$ and $\alpha f$. The residue map of $\alpha$ is the given $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$: reduce $\alpha i=jr$ modulo maximal ideals and use the structural residue isomorphisms of step 1. Thus both maps have maximal-ideal preimage $\mathfrak q$ and induce the identity of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ into the residue field of $T^h$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] makes them equal. On fractions this equality gives $\alpha b=j$, hence $\alpha\beta j=j$. Initiality for $T^h$ gives $\alpha\beta=1$. Therefore $\alpha$ is the required isomorphism with inverse $\beta$, and $\beta j|_C=f$ is precisely its stated characterization.

For $a\in I$, the equality $\alpha i=jr$ gives $\alpha(i(a))=j(\varphi(a))$. Since $\alpha$ is surjective, it sends all finite sums $\sum i(a_
u)x_
u$ onto all sums $\sum j(\varphi(a_
u))y_
u$, so $\alpha(IR^h)=IC\,T^h$. Thus $[x]\mapsto[\alpha(x)]$ and $[y]\mapsto[ eta(y)]$ are well-defined mutually inverse quotient ring maps. On $A/I$ they agree with the structure maps by $\alpha i=jr$; on $C/IC$ they agree because $\alpha f$ is the structural map $C	o T^h$ from step 3. Here the $C/IC$-structure on $R^h/IR^h$ is the one induced by $f$, the pointed map specified in the statement. This explicitly proves both claimed compatibilities.

source.place: Elementary ideal-extension and quotient computation from steps 2-3

proof.text: The extended ideals $IR\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and $(IC)T\subseteq\mathfrak m_T$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-henselization-quotient-at-prime]. It identifies $R^h/IR^h$ and $T^h/IC\,T^h$ as ordinary henselizations of $R/IR$ and $T/(IC)T$. Finally $R/IR\cong(A/I)_{\mathfrak p/I}$ by $[a/s]\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$, with inverse $\bar a/\bar s\mapsto[a/s]$, and identically $T/(IC)T\cong(C/IC)_{\mathfrak q/IC}$. These fraction formulas are well-defined by the localization equality relation and quotient equality, are inverse, and commute with the quotient base maps. They preserve maximal ideals, since a numerator lies in the corresponding prime exactly when its fraction does. Precomposing an initial local map with either local isomorphism preserves its universal property (compose any test local map with the inverse). This proves the final henselization claims under the stated base identifications.
